newsitem.title: UK: Suez Canal expects 100 LNG tankers from Gulf in '9.
newsitem.headline: Suez Canal expects 100 LNG tankers from Gulf in '9.

text.p: Egypt's Suez Canal authority expects a third of the Gulf region's 300 LNG vessels to use the canal for Western destinations this year following its decision to offer a 35 discount for all LNG vessels, the London-based al-Hayat newspaper reported.
It quoted an official as saying the Suez Canal Authority had received positive reactions to the rates from Gulf countries like Oman and Qatar, the main gas producers in the region.

The official said the authority expected 100 LNG vessels to carry seven million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from the Gulf to European and U.S. destinations in 1997. This would be up from 32 LNG tankers in 1996.

The Suez Canal Authority, keen to lure traffic in 1997, announced a package of bargains late last year which it hopes will attract traffic away from alternative routes and back to the strategic waterway linking the Red Sea and the Mediterranean.

Under the measures, loaded northbound tankers are eligible for a 35 percent discount regardless of destination and the same discount is to be granted to the ship upon its ballast southbound trip. Loaded southbound tankers are eligible for a 25 percent discount.
